headline: Given each library its hand-written best practice, a static class with the value on an inline `style`, the field converges toward `vanilla`; next-yak reaches the same shape as a compiler feature, everyone else by writing the split by hand on every dynamic value.

microbench.why: With the static class split from the inline value by hand, the hashers stop regenerating: `cnfast` 0.625 ms/1k, `tailwind-merge` 0.666, `goober` 1.07 all join the fast cluster near `vanilla` (0.614). The css-prop fold, which produces this split automatically, leads at 0.603 ms/1k. The styled perf runtime keeps its `Yak` wrapper at 1.25 ms/1k; `emotion` and `panda` stay back at 2.44 and 2.75 because their idiomatic best practice still serializes.

autocannon.why: Hand-optimized, the utility lanes serve near `vanilla`: `cnfast` 1202 req/s, `tailwind-merge` 1159 against `vanilla`'s 1221 and the css-prop fold's 1279. The styled perf runtime's wrapper holds it to 717; `styled-components`'s `.attrs` inline-style path reaches 634, back in the field it lost in `dyn-translate`.

attribution.why: The hand-written split drops the hashers' library slice: `styled-components`'s `.attrs` path leaves `generateAndInjectStyles` and falls to 0.572 ms library (1.70 ms total) from 3.52 in `dyn-translate`, `goober` to 0.320 ms. `vanilla` and `cnfast` lead at 0.757-0.797 ms. The styled perf runtime still pays its `Yak` wrapper (0.402 ms library, 1.26 ms), so on a single dynamic value it now trails the css-prop fold (0.965 ms) and even `styled-components`.

hydrate.why: The static-class lanes hydrate at 46.9-52.2 ms with the css-prop fold in front. With the dynamic value on inline `style` and the class static, even the hashers stay reasonable, `goober` 83.7 ms, `styled-components` 85.3 ms, far below their `dyn-translate` blowout.

inp.why: Re-rendering one element with a fresh inline value costs ~6.60-7.80 ms across the hand-optimized lanes, a tie; `styled-components`'s `.attrs` path leads at 6.60 ms because it writes only the style attribute. `panda` 13.0 ms and `emotion` 10.8 ms remain the outliers.

mount.why: Cold mount lands at 62.7-68.7 ms for the split lanes with the css-prop fold in front. The hand-written split keeps the hashers' first-inject modest, `styled-components` 83.6 ms, `emotion` 95.5 ms.

renderTiming.why: One recalc per lane; the inline-style split changes where the dynamic value rides, not the browser's recalc count.

payload.why: The css-var split ships 5.24 kB gzipped, under `vanilla` (5.50 kB). The hand-written best-practice lanes ship a static class plus inline styles: `cnfast` 16.8 kB, `tailwind-merge` 15.8 kB, `styled-components` 18.7 kB, mostly their runtime and repeated class bytes.

nsweep.why: Scaling the hand-optimized split to 4000 elements, `cnfast` (2.83 ms) and `tailwind-merge` (2.92) hold near `vanilla` (2.72) and the css-prop fold (2.61). The styled perf runtime's wrapper costs it 5.31 ms; `panda` 12.0 ms and `emotion` 10.1 ms still serialize.

crossCase: `dyn-fair` is the hand-optimized middle of the dynamic trio (`dyn-translate` above is the naive version, `dyn-inline` below the pure inline-style control). Every library reaches near-`vanilla` here only because the developer manually splits the static class from the dynamic inline value, replicating by hand what next-yak's css-var compile does automatically. The parity is real, and so is its price: the same optimization, written per component, on every dynamic value, forever. `dyn-translate` shows what the same code costs when nobody pays that discipline.
